scientific_question: Under a frozen-backbone, fixed-task (SEN12TS-like), fixed-data protocol with only the backbone changed, can ICE derive a task-necessary execution subgraph from a structurally different multisensor foundation model and reduce real compute without changing predictions?

protocol.task: optical-SAR land-cover segmentation (official dense receiver contract)
protocol.data: SEN12TS-like s1(3ch incl ratio) + s2(10ch), T=1 single timestep, 64px@10m
protocol.weights: HuggingFace g-astruc/AnySat models/AnySat.pth (pure encoder, 125.9M params, no pretraining task head in release graph)
protocol.receiver_contract: official AnySat dense usage: concat(final fusion-stack patch tokens, per-modality subpatch)
protocol.method_rule: no artificial deletable layers; receiver built per official usage; ICE must be allowed to return 0% removable compute

preregistered_gates.structural_boundary: <10% or 0% removable compute; recorded as ICE structural boundary, not tampered with to chase numbers

evidence.probe_method: zero-output forward-hook perturbation per executed transformer block; dense output sensitivity threshold 1e-6
evidence.executed_blocks_detail: blocks.0-5 (6) + spatial_encoder.predictor_blocks.0-5 (6), verified via forward hooks; blocks.6 (CrossBlockMulti) invoked via forward_release (invisible to hooks), verified separately: executes once under dense, zeroing changes dense output by 0.555 > 1e-6, hence necessary. Total 13.

conclusion: ICE derives the full graph for AnySat under the official dense contract: 0% of the 13 executed transformer blocks are removable. This is a certified fail-closed outcome, not a pruning failure. AnySat's shared shallow encoder (per-modality 6 layers + global 6+1 fusion) assembles its dense segmentation feature only after the full fusion stack; there is no deep suffix or pretraining head left unread by official downstream usage, unlike CROMA whose 53% savings come from an unread optical deep suffix plus pretraining GAP/joint branches.

interpretation_for_paper.negative_example: AnySat: 0% removable under official dense contract
interpretation_for_paper.claim: ICE efficiency gains are determined by (downstream contract x backbone computation graph), not imposed by ICE. A backbone with no structurally unread compute yields 0% reduction by design; this fail-closed behavior is the method's integrity evidence, distinguishing it from aggressive pruning methods that force a ratio.
interpretation_for_paper.cross_backbone_support: The CROMA/AnySat contrast already supports the paper's core claim that ICE is a dependency compiler rather than a CROMA-specific optimization. A third backbone with a deep suffix or pretraining head (e.g. SkySense-class) would add a second positive data point if pursued.
interpretation_for_paper.caveat: AnySat alone does not provide a second positive efficiency data point; the scientific value here is the structural-boundary negative example plus the architecture-generality of the ICE mechanism (probe + topology layer, P0).
